logs.ROM_COHORT_PLAN.md:
# Bounded Thumb state cohorts (V28 design)

Motivation: V27 removes ~16% of Sky Force outer generated calls, but its first reordered timings are slower. It still flushes/reloads guest registers in each private callee. Test bounded composition retaining those registers across connected Thumb regions; this is an experiment, not an assumed gain.

- Capture Thumb cache emission metadata only while explicitly requested during eager ROM translation. Preserve ordinary finalized bodies for fallback and control.
- Group up to 16 statically connected eager Thumb entries, max 64 KiB original emitted bodies per group. No guest address/game identifiers or profile-derived special cases. ARM, outlined or unsupported emission forms use ordinary base functions.
- Share R0-R14 and split flags in WASM locals. PC/runtime fields retain original per-region publication. At helpers, flush/reload the entire group's cached guest-state union, including fields first used in another region. Reset scratch locals on every constituent entry.
- Iterative dispatch within each group via the immutable mode-tagged map and br_table. No recursive calls, unchanged instruction budget and constituent region cap, immediate outer return after callbacks, pending SVC, zero progress, stop, IRQ or a successor outside the group. RAM remains on validated outer lookup.
- Default off. Same-binary controls plus exact native callback/probe/game gates, full compiler suite, dispatch census, then a fixed four-route reordered timing panel with all observations and startup cost retained. Require repeated gains, not coverage alone.

Review risks: branch-depth relocation; scratch zero initialization; helper-visible union state; flags mutated by callbacks; successor state on short budget; mode switches; invalid map slots; helper return values on WASM operand stack; original block count versus outer generated invocations; typed locals and rejected emitted forms.

## First mechanism result and next review

The V28 speed-policy stationary census has 189,888,189 outer generated entries versus 193,385,263 constituent blocks: only 1.808% stay internal. Its current graph contains local branches/resume points, not the direct BL target computed by the bounded translator. Add that emitted call edge generically, prioritize it before speculative broad-scan entries, and test automatic grouping of a real call/return sequence. Keep the initial census and correctness artifacts separate from the revised graph.

The other structural limit is eager-only coverage: the existing setup translates two library export roots, while many sampled ROM boundaries cross into dynamically compiled ROM libraries. Do not add game/address whitelists. A future bounded hot-ROM group could start at the existing hotness-selected PC and discover a small immutable direct-successor graph, retaining normal outer lookup and cache capacity. It must own its sparse map for the entire worker function lifetime, preserve callback/region/instruction boundaries, and account for duplicated generated code and compilation cost. This is design only, not implemented or a speed claim.

## Further generic opportunities (review only, not applied)

- ARM composition requires typed-local remapping for its i64 prefix and a shared-return wrapper. Keep its existing callback-packed-CPSR semantics, materialize wide flags before exits, and preserve runtime-field writeback. Do not simply enable the Thumb transform for ARM: the current eligibility rejection is intentional.
- Current groups look up a successor even when a translated exit has a statically known target. Emitting direct intra-group transitions could avoid that map work; retain fallback lookup for indirect calls/returns and preserve all short-budget exits. This requires explicit exit metadata, not fragile byte-pattern replacement.
- Dynamic ROM groups could address boundaries outside the two legacy eager libraries without expanding a whitelist. They need bounded discovery, immutable-extent proofs, per-worker map ownership and table-slot release consistent with existing cache lifetime. Do not mix this with state-retention timing before measuring the current candidate.
